newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares hit new records on fresh funds.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares hit new records on fresh funds.

text.p: Russian shares hit a new record in early trade on Thursday as the market processed orders received after the close on Wednesday and traders said they expected further funds later in the day.

The Russian Trading System (RTS) index of 22 shares was a record 381.62 at 0800 GMT after Wednesday's record close of 377.69, although by the early afternoon some shares had retreated from early highs.

"The market closed well yesterday and at the start of the trading we fulfilled orders from New York," IFCI bank deputy stock department head Alexei Abdurakhimov said. "The current levels were reached because there is usually a rise in the West at this time, everyone is in a positive mood. Here no one is selling and people have to buy at offer prices."

He said the rise could peak on Thursday and there will be a price fall either on Friday or on Monday as the growth was due to demand by long-term investors, rather than new money flowing into the market.
"They are long-term investors... I cannot call it new money, I cannot see new money on the market," he said. Sellers were mostly Russian operators.
But Raiffeisen Bank Austria equities trade department head Sergei Sheikov did not rule out a further rise in the next few days.
"It is quite possible that everyone will be suprised to see LUKoil at $18-$19," he said. "There are new investors on the market, who sent about 50 percent of their funds into the blue chips."

LUKoil ordinaries rose to $17.18 at 1000 GMT from $16.80 at Wedneday's close, UES national power company was $0.3295 after $0.3244, Surgutneftegaz oil company ordinaries rose to $1.000 from $0.980 and Sberbank was $295.0 after $270.0.
